item.title: [LU-20505] sanity-lfsck test_5 ldiskfs: Fail to generate linkEA
item.description:
This issue was created by maloo for Andreas Dilger <adilger@dilger.ca>

This issue relates to the following test suite run: https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/807c55f0-d570-446e-81a1-88ab752cee6d

test_5 failed with the following error:

lfs fid2path: cannot find /mnt/lustre [0x200005221:0x53:0x0]: No data available
(13) Fail to generate linkEA: [0x200005221:0x53:0x0]

Test session details:
clients: https://build.whamcloud.com/job/lustre-reviews/127607 - 5.14.0-687.17.1.el9_8.x86_64
servers: https://build.whamcloud.com/job/lustre-reviews/127607 - 5.14.0-687.17.1.el9_8_lustre.x86_64

The mds1 console log reports an -ENOENT error just before the test fails:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_logs/bf470efe-9413-4a7f-b3f5-4dfc6a812649/show_text

mdd_dir_page_build()) lustre-MDT0000-mdtlov: build page failed for [0x200005221:0x1:0x0]: rc = -2

This is failing only on ldiskfs, because this subtest is always skipped on ZFS "OI Scrub not implemented for ZFS"

comments.comment:
This may be a duplicate of LU-20308 and LU-20424 with a different symptom. It is only failing this way on newer kernels (optional test sessions), and most of the time sanity-lfsck test_0 is failing with "Error: '(10) Expect nothing to be repaired, but got: 97'" and then all of the subtests fail until test_5 fails with "Fail to cleanup the env!".

About 7% of the 30% of test_5 failures are caused by this issue, but the lack of linkEA is similar to the missing dirdata in LU-20424.

"wangdi <ddiwang@google.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/67474
Subject: LU-20505 osd-ldiskfs: suppress LMA for OBD_FAIL_FID_IGIF
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: 418c401fd8cfe9da0df249e2b5ee0960afdb0988

adilger  the real reason for this failure is that

"The real reason for the failure is that in test-5, OBD_FAIL_FID_IGIF only suppressed LinkEA and FID-in-dirent, but still wrote the Normal FID into trusted.lma. Consequently, when LFSCK ran after the backup/restore reformat, it detected the existing trusted.lma and reconstructed the LinkEA and dirent using the Normal FID instead of upgrading the file to an IGIF FID. Because the file remained a Normal FID object and the MDT was started without OI scrub, the OI table lacked an entry for this Normal FID, causing subsequent FID-to-path lookups (lfs fid2path) to fail."

 

(The test occasionally passed previously because if the inode mapping happened to remain in OSD's in-memory OI cache (oti_cache), it bypassed the on-disk OI table check; once evicted from cache, subsequent lfs fid2path lookups failed with error 13).

So the patch suppress writing the FID to trusted.lma as well.  But after this fix, it failed with 

== sanity-lfsck test 5: LFSCK can handle IGIF object upgrading ========================================================== 12:09:54 (1786118994)
preparing... 1 * 1 files will be created Fri Aug  7 12:09:57 EDT 2026.
fail_loc=0x1504
total: 1 mkdir in 0.01 seconds: 182.78 ops/second
total: 1 create in 0.01 seconds: 137.88 ops/second
 sanity-lfsck test_5: @@@@@@ FAIL: createmany 1
  Trace dump:
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/test-framework.sh:7496:error()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/sanity-lfsck.sh:94:lfsck_prep()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/sanity-lfsck.sh:656:test_5()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/test-framework.sh:7873:run_one()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/test-framework.sh:7936:run_one_logged()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/test-framework.sh:7750:run_test()
  = /home/green/git/lustre-release/lustre/tests/sanity-lfsck.sh:715:main()

The root cause in lfsck_prep 1 1 1 (analyze by gemini, and looks correct to me)

  1. When createmany -d $DIR/$tdir/d 1 creates directory d0, osd_create() creates the backend inode on disk without trusted.lma. However, the MDT still replies to the client with the Normal FID allocated for the mkdir RPC. The client VFS instantiates and caches the dentry "d0" bound to this Normal FID.
  2. Immediately on the next step, createmany -m $DIR/$tdir/d0/f 1 tries to create file f0 inside d0.
  3. The client VFS path walk traverses into d0 and issues an IT_LOOKUP "d0" RPC to the MDT.
  4. When the MDT looks up d0 on disk, it finds no trusted.lma, so osd_iget_fid() dynamically constructs an IGIF FID [0x0:ino_d0:gen_d0] and returns it in the lookup reply.
  5. The client receives the IGIF FID from the MDT, which collides with the cached dentry in client dcache (already bound to the Normal FID inode). This dentry alias mismatch causes the lookup to fail with -ENOENT (rc = -2).

To make MDT reply igif FID with this fail_loc will need some efforts.  So I wonder do we still support IGIF now? otherwise can we skip this test? It seems not worth the efforts.

"Alex Zhuravlev <bzzz@whamcloud.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/68662
Subject: LU-20505 lfsck: fix osd-scrub vs lfsck race
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: c1f5f5b95446a16e941dcb1d07b7c55d5f56b235

ddiwang the IGIF FIDs are still potentially used if the LMA FIDs are lost, though not normally. However, in this case I'd expect that the dirent found during the lookup contains the original FID, so it should be possible to rebuild the LMA FID from that?
